messages:
anita: heads-up: CI started failing post-deploy for a batch of PRs touching auth middleware. failures show SARIF uploads erroring with impersonation and decrypt failures. blocking a few releases. anyone know what changed?

phil: I rolled a policy cleanup yesterday to remove legacy group members from the `scanner-impersonators` binding. intended to tighten perms, but maybe we removed a group that pipelines relied on.

yasmin: paste the snippets? need to know if it's iam.impersonate or kms.decrypt.

anita: two examples from the pipeline: 
```
ERROR: failed to fetch fixture
cause: iam.credentials.generateAccessToken: PermissionDenied: caller cannot impersonate serviceAccount:scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com

and\n
[sarif-uploader] ERROR: decrypt fixture failed: cloudkms: Decrypt denied for projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/dev/cryptoKeys/fixtures-key
```

ops-bot: audit event recorded: actor=phil@redwood.com action=iam.setPolicy target=projects/redwood/serviceAccounts/scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com timestamp=2026-01-14T02:11:12Z audit_id=AL-20260114-0211. delta: removed member group:legacy-scanners@redwood.com.

phil: that matches. I removed legacy-scanners and assumed scanners-team had already been propagated. looks like some pipelines still reference the old group.

yasmin: short-term mitigation: create an ephemeral grant for the uploader job to allow impersonation + kms.decrypt for fixture key. prefer not to revert policy.

ops-bot: ephemeral grant issued: grant_id=EG-20260114-19 principal=group:legacy-scanners@redwood.com role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator expires=2026-01-14T04:20:00Z. request logged.

anita: re-ran blocked jobs; SARIF uploads succeeded after grant. thanks.

yasmin: follow-ups (action items):
1) infra PR to map scanner pipelines explicitly to `serviceAccount:scanner@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and avoid group indirection (phil).
2) add a keystore & impersonation smoke test job that runs when any IAM change touches service accounts or keyring resources (yasmin). smoke should attempt a short-lived token + KMS decrypt against a sample fixture.
3) update suppression rules: require `owner` and `expiry` metadata and allow fingerprint fallback if SARIF missing (security).
4) export full audit window and attach to incident for postmortem (anita).

phil: opened infra#821 with the explicit-service-account binding and terraform plan. includes a follow-up to deprecate group-based bindings.

ops-bot: smoke-run scheduled: smoke-20260114-01 queued.

yasmin: for the fingerprint fallback, propose collector compute fingerprint = sha256(normalize(message)+file_path+tokenized_context_3). then map suppressions by fingerprint first, ruleId second. reduces vendor churn impact.

sec-bot: recommended postmortem fields: timeline, audit_ids, grant_id, infra PR link, smoke run id, suppression mapping csv. created ticket SEC-2026-01-14-01. severity: low-medium.

anita: also suggest adding a pre-merge policy: any PR that changes IAM on keyrings or service accounts must include a green smoke-run and `approval:security` label. will add to the secure-sdlc checklist.

phil: agreed. I'll fast-track infra#821 review and include documentation on why explicit SA binding is safer for impersonation chains.

yasmin: scheduling collector change to compute fingerprints and backfill mappings over the weekend. will post progress.

anita: thanks all — incident mitigated for now. final postmortem to include owner notifications for suppressed findings that became unannotated during the outage.
